rationale: The one substantive ground-truth inline concern (the RoPE test's dependence on a duplicated-half freq layout, already fixed in this diff snapshot) is echoed by both candidates via the shared rope.py duplicate-half-invariant finding, so recall is close and modest for both since GT is otherwise mostly process chatter (merge conflicts, readiness) that X alone investigated. X's findings are uniformly backed by explicit evidence citations (grep/CI/commit-diff tool output), making them easy to verify and low-fabrication-risk, whereas Y's review — while containing one genuinely valuable, correctly-triaged blocking finding (the RMSNorm default-dtype regression breaking other models) — leans on highly specific unverifiable GPU benchmark numbers presented with no shown provenance, raising real fabrication risk. Y's clearer blocking/perf/correctness triage and ready-to-apply fixes edge out X on actionability, but X's broader, better-grounded coverage narrowly wins overall.
